column3: Four commercial cello G2 strings (nominal 98 Hz): D'Addario Prelude, D'Addario Helicore, Thomastik-Infeld Dominant Cello and D'Addario Kaplan; the paper says other information on how they are made is unavailable because of manufacturer confidentiality
column4: Rigid monochord with a playing length of 0.70 m; linear density l = T/(2 L f0)^2 from the measured tension and fundamental; bending stiffness B from a fit of f_n/n = f0 + c n^2 to the inharmonic spacing of the natural frequencies of breaking-wire pluck responses, B = 2 c T L^2/(f0 pi^2), points beyond a z-score of 3 excluded; the mean quality factor over the first 30 modes from the pluck decays (fits with R^2 below 0.98 excluded); 12-15 plucks per string
column5: The printed +- are the standard deviation of repeated measurements of the string through the experiment (the string was not retuned during the bowing measurements); Q as a function of mode number is a figure and is not in this pack; the Dominant's own paper (Acta Acustica 2024) says it has a synthetic core and chrome winding

column3: A Thomastik-Infeld Dominant medium-gauge cello G string, which the paper says has a synthetic core and chrome winding, mounted on rigid supports
column4: Tension and fundamental frequency measured right after the first measurement session, scale length and diameter measured, linear density l = T/(2 L f0)^2, impedance Z = sqrt(l T); bending stiffness from three plucked-string signals by the wire-breaking method after the session
column5: Another session of the same string type as the JASA Express Letters table (116.1 N here against 116.3 +- 0.7 N there); the printed +- of B is as the paper gives it and its basis is not restated in the table

column3: DERIVED row, not a measurement: the Thomastik-Infeld Dominant cello G string of lampis-jasael-2024 (Lampis, Mayer, Chatziioannou, JASA Express Letters 4, 113201 (2024), Table 1, string C). The paper prints one loss number for it: the quality factor averaged over the first 30 modes from the breaking-wire pluck decays, Q_hat = 1064. Its per-mode Q values are only plotted (Fig. 1 left, with a Valette-model fit whose parameters are not printed in the text).
column4: Constant-loss reading chosen by the swarm orchestrator (MagentaBadger, mail id 144, 2026-11-03) and applied by PinkLantern: eta_F = eta_B = 1/Q_hat = 9.398496240601504e-4, so that the engine's zeta_k = (T eta_F + EI eta_B k^2) / (2 (T + EI k^2)) (Woodhouse, Acta Acustica united with Acustica 90 (2004) eq. (8), constant factors, eta_A omitted because the renderer computes air drag) equals 1/(2 Q_hat) for every mode and Q_k = 1064 exactly. The engine requires two distinct strictly positive loss rows, so eta_B = 0 is not admissible and both rows carry the same value.
column5: A mean over 30 modes does not identify a frequency dependence; the plotted per-mode Q is not used; this row does not reproduce the Dominant's decay mode by mode, and it says nothing about loss in the bow contact. Experiment pack (pack_id cello-g-strings-whole-lampis-2024-lossq), derived by PinkLantern for MB's GO 1; the repository seed pack is unchanged and nothing is landed.
